laura_cs: AcmeHealth reporting a regression after yesterday's quant rollout. Their quantized endpoint (gptj-4b, 4-bit calibrated) p95 jumped ~140ms -> ~420ms. Small prompts are slower than fp16 baseline. They want a fast mitigation and a clear customer note. cc @sam_runtime @devon_oncall

sam_runtime: Do we have pool/host info and the exact model variant? Any traffic shift or batching change?

laura_cs: Dedicated pool 'dedicated-acme-1', model tag 'gptj-4b-4bit-calib-v3'. No traffic spike reported, steady 0.8 rps per host. Posted kernel log snippets and endpoint config:```
model_variant: gptj-4b-4bit-calib-v3
routing_policy: prefer_quant_when_compatible
batching_window_ms: 10
kv_prefetch: enabled
calib_on_request: true
```

devon_oncall: Oof — `calib_on_request: true` stands out. That can trigger per-request calibration passes on cold KV cache. Can you grab a perf profile for a single small request (prompt 12 tokens) and a 128-token request? Also dump kv cache stats (hit rate / warmup).

laura_cs: Pasting simplified profiler outputs (captured with runtime profiler v2):
```
-- 12-token request (tail): total=190ms
matmul_int4_fallback_v1      72ms (38%)
attention_fp16_kv_build      54ms (28%)
calibration_pass_sample      35ms (18%)
kv_prefetch_wait             18ms (9%)
overhead_rpc_dispatch        11ms (6%)
-- 128-token request: total=410ms
matmul_int4_fallback_v1     160ms (39%)
attention_fp16_kv_build     110ms (27%)
calibration_pass_sample      95ms (23%)
kv_prefetch_wait             25ms (6%)
```
kv stats: `kv_cache_warm_keys=0.12, kv_prefetch_attempts=24, kv_prefetch_success=3`

sam_runtime: Interesting — two red flags: 1) `matmul_int4_fallback_v1` is a slow fallback kernel (we saw regressions last quarter when kernel selection picks fallback vs optimized int4 path), 2) `calibration_pass_sample` is doing a runtime calibration step per request. That explains the 18-23% overhead.

mike_ml: On the calibration side: we introduced `calib_on_request` as a temporary safety net during onboarding, but it should be disabled for production dedicated pools. When enabled it does a dynamic per-layer percentile pass over a sample batch which is expensive if not cached. We expected it to run once per model load, not every request — looks like there's a bug where the `calib_state` wasn't persisted to the pool metadata on warmup.

devon_oncall: Mitigations: immediate -> disable `calib_on_request` on the customer's pool and force reuse of compiled kernels; short -> rollback that pool to fp16 variant; medium -> patch kernel selector to prefer the optimized int4 path and add assert to persist calib_state after warmup.

sam_runtime: I can push a routing override to prefer `gptj-4b-fp16-v2` for `dedicated-acme-1` now (non-disruptive, routes new requests). Devon, can you coordinate a fast rollback if needed?

laura_cs: Customer wants an ETA and temporary SLA assurance. If we route to fp16 they will accept degraded cost for latency fix. Please confirm ETA for routing change and a follow-up fix timeline.

devon_oncall: Routing override -> 5 minutes. I'll prepare a canary rollback to fp16 for the entire pool if override doesn't help within 15m. Patch for persisting calib_state + unit tests -> PR by EOD, deploy in next build (estimated 24-36h). Kernel selector change -> deeper; target next week.

sam_runtime: Quick runbook I'm going to follow: 1) apply routing override to fp16 (5m) 2) toggle `calib_on_request=false` on pool metadata (5m) 3) monitor p95 & kv hitrate for 30m 4) if p95 still >200ms, initiate pool rollback to fp16 variant (devon) 5) communicate to customer within 30m with actions taken.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: starting routing override to model 'gptj-4b-fp16-v2' for pool 'dedicated-acme-1' (request id: d0a3f2)

laura_cs: Thanks — I'll draft the customer message: short note explaining we observed runtime calibration and a fallback kernel causing extra CPU/GPU time, steps we're taking (routing to FP16, disabling runtime calibration, monitoring), and ETA. Will share for review.

mike_ml: Also recommend we schedule an offline calibration job to precompute quant params and store them in model metadata for this customer's pool. That will avoid re-running the expensive sample pass and allow safe re-enabling of quant later.

devon_oncall: Agreed. Action owners: sam -> routing override + toggle `calib_on_request` (now), laura -> customer comms (30m), devon -> rollback plan if needed and patch release coordination, mike -> offline calibration job & follow-up doc. Will update this thread with metrics after 30m.

laura_cs: Sending customer note now, will update when they ack. :white_check_mark:

sam_runtime: override applied, `calib_on_request` set false on pool metadata. Monitoring p95...

laura_cs: Customer acked, appreciates fast response and accepted fp16 fallback for short term.

sam_runtime: Early numbers: p95 dropped from ~420ms -> ~160ms within 8m. kv_cache_warm_keys improved to 0.48 after some warm traffic. Keeping monitoring for 30m.

devon_oncall: Closing initial escalation. We'll file follow-ups: 1) bug for calib_state persistence, 2) improve kernel selector heuristics, 3) add alert when `calib_on_request` is true for prod pools.

laura_cs: Thanks everyone. I'll post a short summary to the customer and internal postmortem channel once we have the PR links and rollback notes.
